faqs.q: What is the typical hourly rate for a trade assistant in Australia?
faqs.a: Trade assistant rates vary by award and experience. The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour for permanent employees, while many trade assistants are covered by awards such as the Manufacturing Award or Building and Construction Award, which set higher minimum rates. Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top, making the casual minimum $33.05 per hour. For precise rates, check the relevant award pay guide on the Fair Work Ombudsman website.

faqs.q: How do I calculate my annual trade assistant salary from an hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52 weeks. For a full-time trade assistant working 38 hours per week, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52 = annual gross salary. For example, at $30 per hour, the annual figure is $30 × 38 × 52 = $59,280. This assumes no unpaid overtime, penalty rates or allowances.

faqs.q: Is superannuation included in my trade assistant salary?
faqs.a: No, superannuation is paid on top of your salary. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee rate is 12% of your ordinary earnings, up to a maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Trade Assistant Salary in Australia

If you're working as a trade assistant or considering a role in this field, you'll often see pay advertised as an hourly rate. Converting that hourly figure into an annual **trade assistant salary** helps you compare offers, budget for the year, and understand your tax obligations. This guide explains how to do the maths, what the Fair Work Ombudsman says about minimum rates, and how casual loading and superannuation affect your total compensation.

### How to Calculate Annual Pay from an Hourly Rate

The standard formula for converting an hourly rate to annual gross pay is:

**Hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks = annual salary**

For full-time work, we assume 38 hours per week, which is the ordinary hours under most modern awards and the National Employment Standards. For example, if your hourly rate is $30.00, your annual gross pay would be:

$30.00 × 38 × 52 = $59,280

If you work part-time or irregular hours, adjust the weekly hours accordingly. The same formula works for any weekly hours. You can also find your fortnightly pay by multiplying your weekly pay by 2. For the example above, weekly pay is $1,140, so fortnightly pay is $2,280 before tax.

### The Role of Awards and the National Minimum Wage

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours, according to the Fair Work Ombudsman. Award minimum wages increased by 4.75% from the same date. Many trade assistants are covered by awards such as the Manufacturing Award or the Building and Construction General On-site Award, which set higher minimum rates than the National Minimum Wage. Always check the specific award that applies to your job using the [pay guides](/blog) on the Fair Work Ombudsman website.

If you are not covered by an award or enterprise agreement, the National Minimum Wage is the legal floor. However, most trade assistants earn above this due to skill demands and industry standards. The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports that full-time adult average weekly ordinary time earnings were $2,083.70 in May 2026, which equates to roughly $54.83 per hour for a 38-hour week. This gives context for what a typical trade assistant salary might be in the broader market.

### Casual Loading and Superannuation

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave. For a trade assistant on the National Minimum Wage, the casual rate is $33.05 per hour ($26.44 × 1.25). When using our [timesheet](/), you can check a box to add the 25% casual loading to your base rate. **Do not enter a rate that already includes casual loading** – the tool adds it automatically.

Superannuation is paid on top of your salary. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee rate is 12% of your ordinary earnings, up to a maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For example, on a $60,000 annual salary, your employer contributes an extra $7,200 into your super fund. This is not part of your take-home pay but is a valuable part of your total remuneration package. Learn more about [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

### Tax and Medicare on Your Trade Assistant Salary

Your annual gross pay is the starting point for calculating tax. The Australian Taxation Office uses the 2026–27 resident tax rates:

- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% on the excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: $4,020 plus 30% on the excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: $31,020 plus 37% on the excess over $135,000
- $190,001 and over: $51,370 plus 45% on the excess over $190,000

In addition, the Medicare levy of 2% applies to most taxpayers. For the 2025–26 year, single taxpayers with a taxable income below $24,276 pay no Medicare levy, with a phase-in up to $30,345. These thresholds are used here as the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) guide to see how tax and Medicare affect your net income.

For a trade assistant earning $60,000 annually, the estimated tax (including Medicare) would be roughly $9,667, leaving a take-home pay of about $50,333 per year, or $967 per week. This is an estimate only – it does not include HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging.

### Using the Timesheet Tool

Our [timesheet](/)
 allows you to enter your base hourly rate and see the annual, fortnightly, and weekly figures instantly. You can toggle casual loading on or off, and the tool applies the correct super and tax calculations based on the latest rates. It's a quick way to understand your trade assistant salary in full context, from gross pay to what lands in your bank account.

Remember: the annual figure is your hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. For a precise determination of your pay and entitlements, refer to your award or enterprise agreement and consult the Fair Work Ombudsman.
